questions.q:
Consider the following statements about State Legislative Councils:
1. Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council by law after the Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.
2. At present six States have Legislative Councils.
3. A law creating or abolishing a Council is treated as an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 169 lets Parliament act by a simple-majority law, and clause (3) says that such a law is not an amendment under Article 368. The six States with Councils are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the composition of a Legislative Council are correct?
1. One-third of the members are elected by members of the Legislative Assembly.
2. One-twelfth of the members are elected by graduates.
3. One-twelfth of the members are elected by teachers.
4. One-third of the members are nominated by the Governor.
questions.e: The Governor nominates one-sixth (persons with special knowledge of literature, science, art, the cooperative movement and social service), not one-third. One-third each comes from the MLAs and from local bodies, and one-twelfth each from graduates and teachers.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (Legislative Council); Art 171

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the size and membership of a Legislative Council:
1. A person must be at least 25 years old to be a member.
2. Its strength cannot exceed one-third of the strength of the Legislative Assembly.
3. Its strength cannot be less than 40.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 171 sets the ceiling at one-third of the Assembly and a floor of 40 members, and Article 173 requires a minimum age of 30 for the Council (25 for the Assembly). An Assembly member needs to be only 25.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Legislative Council of a State is a continuing House that cannot be dissolved.
Statement-II: One-third of its members retire every second year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Members serve six-year terms, and since a third retire every two years the House always has experienced members and is never wholly renewed. This is the same pattern as in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q:
How many of the following State-Assembly strength pairs are correctly matched?
1. Sikkim : 32
2. Goa : 40
3. Mizoram : 60
4. Arunachal Pradesh : 40
questions.e: Sikkim has 32 and Goa 40; Mizoram has 40 and Arunachal Pradesh has 60. Article 170 sets the general range at 60 to 500, with small States such as Sikkim, Goa and Mizoram as exceptions.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (Legislative Assembly); Art 170

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A person cannot be a member of both Houses of the State Legislature at the same time.
2. The minimum age for election to the Legislative Assembly is 25 years.
3. A person elected to both Parliament and a State Legislature must resign from one within 14 days of the result, failing which the Parliament seat becomes vacant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 190 bars membership of both Houses of a State Legislature, and the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950 apply to dual membership of Parliament and a State Legislature. If the person does not resign from the State seat within 14 days, his Parliament seat becomes vacant.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of a Legislative Assembly:
1. The Speaker is elected by the Assembly from among its members.
2. When a resolution for the Speaker's removal is under consideration, the Speaker may preside but cannot vote.
3. The Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 178 and 179 provide for election and vacation, and removal needs a resolution by a majority of all members after 14 days' notice. Article 181 bars the Speaker from presiding when his own removal is under consideration, though he may speak and vote in the first instance.

questions.q: The Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State is
o: The Chief Minister of the State
Elected by the Council from among its members
questions.e: Article 182 provides for the Council to choose its own Chairman and Deputy Chairman. Unlike the Rajya Sabha, where the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman, the Council's presiding officer is one of its own members.

questions.q: A Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly (an ordinary Bill) is rejected by the Legislative Council. Assembly passes it again, and the Council delays it again. The maximum period for which the Council can delay such a Bill is
o: Four months (three months, then one month)
questions.e: Under Article 197 the Council can delay for three months the first time and one month the second time. The Assembly's will ultimately prevails, as there is no joint sitting in the States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a Money Bill in a State Legislature:
1. It can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly.
2. The Speaker's certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is final.
3. The Legislative Council can reject it within 14 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 198 allows the Council only to return the Bill with recommendations within 14 days; the Assembly can accept or reject them, and the Bill is deemed passed after 14 days. Article 199(3) makes the Speaker's decision final.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (Legislative Procedure); Arts 198, 199

questions.q:
Which of the following powers does the Governor have in respect of an ordinary Bill passed by the State Legislature?
1. To give assent
2. To withhold assent
3. To return a Money Bill for reconsideration
4. To reserve the Bill for the President's consideration
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Article 200 lets the Governor assent, withhold assent, return a Bill (other than a Money Bill) with a message, or reserve it for the President. A Money Bill cannot be returned.

questions.q: Under Article 200 of the Constitution, the Governor MUST reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President if it
o: levies a tax on agricultural income
derogates from the powers of the High Court so as to endanger its constitutional position
changes the salaries of the State Ministers
creates a new district in the State
questions.e: The second proviso to Article 200 makes reservation compulsory for such a Bill, to safeguard the High Court's position. For other Bills reservation is discretionary.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ordinance-making power of the Governor under Article 213:
1. An ordinance remains in force indefinitely till the Governor withdraws it.
2. It can be exercised when the Legislative Assembly (or both Houses) is not in session.
3. Certain ordinances require the prior instructions of the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Ordinance must be laid before the Legislature and ceases to operate six weeks after it reassembles, or earlier if disapproved. Prior instructions are required for ordinances that need the President's previous sanction for introducing a Bill.

questions.q: In Nabam Rebia v Deputy Speaker (2016), which concerned the Arunachal Pradesh Assembly, the Supreme Court held that
o: a Governor may advance the Assembly session at his discretion without the advice of the Council of Ministers
the Tenth Schedule does not apply to States in the North-East
a Speaker cannot decide disqualification petitions while a notice for his own removal is pending
a Deputy Speaker has no power to preside over the Assembly in any circumstances
questions.e: The Constitution Bench held that a Speaker facing a removal notice would lack the confidence of the House and cannot adjudicate on disqualification meanwhile. It also held that the Governor's power to summon the House under Article 174 must ordinarily be exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
questions.s: Supreme Court, Nabam Rebia (2016); Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tenth Schedule:
1. It was added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
2. A nominated member can join any political party at any time without disqualification.
3. An independent member is disqualified if he joins a political party after his election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A nominated member who joins a party within six months of taking his seat is safe; joining after that period leads to disqualification. The Schedule thus penalises changing allegiance after the voters or nominating authority have chosen the member.

questions.q:
How many of the following changes were introduced by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
1. Omission of the provision protecting a 'split' of one-third of a legislature party.
2. A ceiling on the Council of Ministers at 10 per cent of the Lower House.
3. A minimum of 20 ministers in a State.
4. Disqualification of defectors from holding remunerative political posts.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The ceiling is 15 per cent (not 10) of the strength of the Lok Sabha or the State Assembly, and the minimum in a State is 12 (not 20) ministers.

questions.q: Under the Tenth Schedule, the members of a legislature party would NOT be disqualified if
o: one-third of the legislature party leaves to form a separate group
a member votes against the party whip without permission and the party refuses to condone it
not less than two-thirds of the legislature party agree to merge with another political party
a member resigns from the party and contests as an independent
questions.e: Paragraph 4 protects mergers backed by two-thirds of the legislature party. The earlier protection for a one-third split was deleted by the 91st Amendment, and resignation from the party does constitute voluntary giving up of membership.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Anti-defection chapter; Tenth Schedule para 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kihoto Hollohan v Zachillhu (1992):
1. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the Tenth Schedule.
2. Paragraph 7, barring the courts' jurisdiction, was struck down for lack of ratification by half of the States.
3. The Speaker's decision on disqualification is open to limited judicial review.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held that the Speaker acts as a tribunal in the matter, so his decision can be reviewed for jurisdictional errors, mala fides and the like. Paragraph 7 had altered the courts' jurisdiction and thus needed ratification under Article 368(2).
questions.s: Supreme Court, Kihoto Hollohan (1992); Laxmikanth, Anti-defection chapter

questions.q: In Keisham Meghachandra Singh v Speaker, Manipur Legislative Assembly (2020), the Supreme Court
o: held that the Speaker has unlimited time to decide petitions
held that courts can never review the Speaker's decisions
suggested that Parliament consider an independent tribunal to decide disqualification and said Speakers should decide petitions within three months
questions.e: The Court was concerned that Speakers belonging to ruling parties delay decisions. It held that, absent exceptional circumstances, petitions should be decided within three months.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi:
1. Article 239AA was inserted by the 69th Amendment in 1991.
2. The Assembly has 70 seats.
3. The Assembly can make laws on police, public order and land.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Delhi's Assembly can legislate on State and Concurrent List subjects except police, public order and land, which remain with the Union. This special arrangement distinguishes Delhi from a full State.

questions.q: In the case on control over services in Delhi (Government of NCT of Delhi v Union of India, 2023), a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that
o: the elected Delhi Government has control over services other than police, public order and land
the Lieutenant Governor has control over all services in Delhi
Delhi has no legislative power over any State List subject
the Union Government has exclusive control over all services in Delhi
questions.e: The Court held that the elected Government must have control of the administrative services, to uphold the principle of collective responsibility to the legislature. Parliament later enacted the GNCTD (Amendment) Act 2023 that altered this position.
questions.s: Supreme Court, 11 May 2023; Laxmikanth, Union Territories chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following sets contains all the Union Territories that have a Legislative Assembly?
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Chandigarh
questions.e: Delhi (Article 239AA), Puducherry (Government of Union Territories Act 1963) and Jammu and Kashmir (Reorganisation Act 2019) have Assemblies. Ladakh and Chandigarh do not.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Union Territories chapter; J&K Reorganisation Act 2019

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delimitation Commission for Jammu and Kashmir (2020-22):
1. It increased the number of Assembly seats from 83 to 90.
2. Six of the additional seats went to the Jammu division and one to the Kashmir division.
3. It provided reserved seats for Scheduled Tribes for the first time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission, chaired by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, fixed 90 seats with 43 in Jammu and 47 in Kashmir, plus the seats kept for Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Nine seats were reserved for STs.
questions.s: PIB, 5 May 2022; Delimitation Commission J&K (final order)

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about delimitation in India are correct?
1. Delimitation Commissions for the whole country were constituted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002.
2. The orders of the Delimitation Commission have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court.
3. The Delimitation Commission of 2002 was constituted under the Delimitation Act, 2002.
4. Parliament can modify the final orders of the Commission.
questions.e: Commissions were set up in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, and Article 329(a) bars courts from questioning their orders. The orders are final and cannot be altered even by Parliament, which is why the commission is the guardian of fair constituencies.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Parliament chapter; Art 329, Delimitation Act 2002

questions.q: The quorum for a meeting of a State Legislative Assembly is
o: One-tenth of the total members of the House or ten members, whichever is greater
questions.e: Article 189(3) fixes this quorum; it includes the presiding officer. In the absence of a quorum, the presiding officer must adjourn or suspend the meeting.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the privileges of the State Legislature:
1. The Governor, being a part of the Legislature, enjoys the privileges as a member.
2. Article 194 guarantees freedom of speech in the Legislature.
3. No member is liable in any court for anything said or any vote given in the Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The privileges are available to members and those who speak in the House, such as the Advocate General and ministers. The Governor is part of the legislature (Article 168) but does not enjoy these privileges.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 211 bars discussion in the State Legislature on the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge in discharge of his duties.
2. Article 212 bars judicial review of every legislative proceeding, including illegality.
3. Article 212 says that the validity of proceedings in the Legislature cannot be questioned on the ground of an alleged irregularity of procedure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 212 protects against challenges on procedural irregularity only. The Supreme Court (Raja Ram Pal, 2007) held that proceedings that are illegal or unconstitutional remain open to scrutiny.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter; Arts 211, 212; Raja Ram Pal (2007)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Members of a State Legislative Council do not participate in the election of the President of India.
Statement-II: The Electoral College consists only of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 54 keeps the Councils out of the Electoral College because the Presidential election is meant to reflect the popular will through directly elected members. The same Article leaves out nominated members.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Legislative Council of a State with the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Council has no role in electing members of the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Chairman of the Council is elected from its members, whereas the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President.
3. The Council can delay an ordinary Bill for up to six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Council can delay an ordinary Bill by at most four months and has no joint-sitting mechanism, unlike the Rajya Sabha, which can delay for six months and force a joint sitting. In the State, the Assembly has the final say.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (comparison with Parliament)

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT provided for in the case of the State Legislatures?
o: Passing of Money Bills only in the Assembly
Delay of an ordinary Bill by the Council
A joint sitting of the two Houses to resolve a deadlock on a Bill
Reservation of a Bill by the Governor for the President
questions.e: The Constitution gives the Assembly the final say if the Houses differ, so no joint-sitting provision exists. A joint sitting exists only for Parliament under Article 108.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (comparison with Parliament)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the repugnancy between Union and State laws under Article 254:
1. If a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with a Union law, the Union law prevails.
2. A State law reserved for the President and given his assent can prevail in that State.
3. Parliament can later enact a law on the same matter, overriding the State law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 254(1) gives the Union law priority; 254(2) lets a State law with Presidential assent prevail locally. The proviso allows Parliament to override it with a later law, even on the same matter.

questions.q: The Supreme Court in Lily Thomas v Union of India (2013) struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which
o: allowed a legislator to vote while in custody
allowed a convicted legislator to continue in office for three months or during appeal
imposed a lifetime ban on all convicted persons
exempted legislators from disqualification for corruption
questions.e: Under Section 8 of the Act, a legislator convicted and sentenced to two or more years is disqualified. After this ruling, the protection of continuing in office pending appeal was removed, so disqualification takes effect from the date of conviction.
questions.s: Supreme Court, Lily Thomas (2013); Laxmikanth, Parliament chapter

questions.q: A member of a State Legislature who is absent from all meetings for sixty days without the permission of the House may have his seat declared vacant. In calculating this period,
o: any period during which the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days is excluded
any period of adjournment is included
only the period of sittings is included
the period of prorogation is included
questions.e: Article 190(4) excludes the days of prorogation and adjournment for more than four consecutive days from the 60-day count. This gives members protection when the House is not meeting for long stretches.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the budget in a State Legislature:
1. The Legislative Council votes on the demands for grants but cannot reject the Money Bill.
2. The Annual Financial Statement is laid before both Houses under Article 202.
3. The Contingency Fund of the State is held by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only the Assembly votes on demands; the Council can discuss the budget but cannot vote on the demands (Article 203). The Contingency Fund of the State is at the Governor's disposal under Article 267(2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's address to the State Legislature:
1. The Governor addresses the Legislature at the first session after each general election and at the first session of every year.
2. The Governor can nominate Anglo-Indian members to the Assembly.
3. The address reflects the policy of the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 176 provides for the address, in which the Governor informs the Legislature about the reasons for summoning it; the text is prepared by the government. The nomination of Anglo-Indians ended with the 104th Amendment.

questions.q: A member expelled from his political party continues to belong to that party for the purposes of the Tenth Schedule. This was held by the Supreme Court in
o: Rajendra Singh Rana v Swami Prasad Maurya (2007)
G. Viswanathan v Speaker, Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly (1996)
questions.e: The Court held that an expelled member who later joins another party attracts disqualification, because expulsion does not end his membership of the original party for this purpose. It closed the loophole of being expelled and then joining another group.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the dismissal of State governments and the Supreme Court's ruling in S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994):
1. A Proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review.
2. A Proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months.
3. The State Assembly may be dissolved before Parliament approves the Proclamation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held that the Assembly may only be suspended until Parliament approves the Proclamation, and dissolution before that is unconstitutional. It also held that the use of Article 356 is open to review and that federalism and secularism are basic features.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, President's Rule chapter; S.R. Bommai (1994)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reservation of seats in legislatures:
1. Women's reservation under Article 332A is already in operation.
2. Article 332 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies.
3. The 104th Amendment extended this reservation up to 2030 and ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 104th Amendment (effective January 2020) extended SC/ST reservation by ten years and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. Article 332A, from the 106th Amendment, will operate only after delimitation.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Parliament/State Legislature chapters; 104th and 106th Amendments

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Statement-II: The Legislative Council can pass a vote of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Under Article 164(2) the Council of Ministers answers to the elected Assembly, which alone can remove the government by a no-confidence vote. The Legislative Council can discuss and question, but has no power to defeat the government.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the abolition and revival of Legislative Councils:
1. Punjab and West Bengal abolished their Councils in 1969.
2. Tamil Nadu abolished its Council in 1986.
3. Andhra Pradesh abolished its Council in 1985 and revived it in 2007.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Councils are created or abolished by an Act of Parliament on the State's resolution under Article 169. The history shows that the political party in power often shapes the decision.

questions.q: A member of a State Legislative Assembly votes against the direction of his party without permission, but the party condones the act within fifteen days. Under the Tenth Schedule, the member
o: is disqualified as soon as he votes against the whip
is disqualified unless the Speaker permits him to continue
is disqualified if the vote changes the outcome of the House
questions.e: Paragraph 2(1)(b) disqualifies a member who votes or abstains contrary to a party direction without permission, unless the vote is condoned within 15 days. The remedy lies with the party, not the Speaker.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Anti-defection chapter; Tenth Schedule para 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the term and sessions of a State Legislative Assembly:
1. Its normal term is five years.
2. The Governor can prorogue the House but only the Speaker can dissolve it.
3. During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend it by one year at a time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 172 provides a five-year term and, during Emergency, Parliament's one-year extension. The Governor, not the Speaker, summons, prorogues and dissolves the Assembly under Article 174.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Subject) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Article 168
B. Article 169
C. Article 170
D. Article 171
List-II
1. Composition of Legislative Assemblies
2. Constitution of Legislatures in States
3. Composition of Legislative Councils
4. Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils
questions.e: The sequence follows the logic of the chapter: Art 168 sets up the Legislature, 169 deals with Councils' abolition or creation, 170 with the Assembly's composition and 171 with the Council's composition.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their enactment:
1. 52nd Amendment (Tenth Schedule)
2. 91st Amendment (Anti-defection changes)
3. 69th Amendment (Delhi)
4. 104th Amendment (SC/ST reservation extended)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment came in 1985, the 69th in 1991, the 91st in 2003 and the 104th in 2019 (effective 2020).

questions.q: Under Article 210 of the Constitution, business in the State Legislature shall be transacted in
o: Any language of the Eighth Schedule chosen by the member
the official language(s) of the State or in Hindi or English, subject to the presiding officer's permission to use the mother tongue
questions.e: Article 210 allows the State's official language or languages, Hindi or English, and the presiding officer may permit a member who cannot express himself in these to speak in his mother tongue. Unlike Parliament, the Legislature may use the State's language.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Council of Ministers in a State:
1. A person who is not a member of the Legislature can be appointed minister but must become a member within six months.
2. The total number of ministers shall not exceed 15 per cent of the strength of the Assembly.
3. A person can continue as a minister without being a member of the Legislature indefinitely.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 164(4) allows a non-member to be a minister for six months and the 91st Amendment limited the size to 15 per cent, with a minimum of 12 in a State. A non-member who fails to get elected within six months must cease to be a minister.

questions.q: For the purpose of electing members to the Legislative Council from the teachers' constituency, a person must have been engaged for at least three years in teaching in
o: an educational institution not lower in standard than a secondary school
questions.e: Teachers' constituencies cover those teaching for three years in institutions not lower than secondary school; graduates' constituencies need a graduate of at least three years' standing. They reflect the idea of representing educated professions.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, State Legislature chapter (Legislative Council); Art 171, RPA

questions.q:
Statement-I: A nominated member of a Legislative Assembly is disqualified if he joins a political party after the expiry of six months from the date he takes his seat.
Statement-II: An independently elected member is disqualified if he joins any political party after his election.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct under Paragraph 2(2) and 2(3), but they are separate rules applying to different categories of members. The six-month window for nominated members does not explain the rule for elected independents.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Anti-defection chapter; Tenth Schedule para 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bills in a State Legislature:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced in the Legislative Council with the Governor's recommendation.
2. A Money Bill can be introduced only on the recommendation of the Governor.
3. A Financial Bill of the second category can be introduced in either House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 207 requires the Governor's recommendation for Money Bills and for Financial Bills of the first category, and these must start in the Assembly (Article 198). Category II Financial Bills can start in either House; the Governor's recommendation is needed for their consideration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the conduct of business in a State Legislature:
1. All questions are decided by a majority of members present and voting, the presiding officer voting only in the case of a tie.
2. A meeting can be held only when all the members are present.
3. Proceedings are not invalid merely because of a vacancy in the membership or because an unqualified person sat or voted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 189 allows the House to act despite vacancies, which protects legislative work from technical challenges. Only the quorum (one-tenth of the members or ten) is needed, not full attendance.
